newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended up at a two-year high close of 8.2905 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2914 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to speculative buying a few minutes before trading ceased, traders said.
The close was the highest since May 18, 1995 when the yuan ended at 8.2892.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2914.

The yuan opened unchanged at an intraday low of 8.2914 and rose slightly to move around 8.2910 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2903. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2910, traders said.
One dealer said the yuan moved steadily around the 8.2910 level for most of the session and only speculative buying in the last few minutes pushed it higher.
"Speculators made use of strong pro-yuan sentiment to buy in late trading, making the yuan close much higher," he said. "A lack of intervention by the central bank also helped."
A second dealer said dull trading exaggerated the yuan's movement on Wednesday.
"The yuan's rise today was not supported by volume," he said. "The market widely expects the central bank to intervene to depress the yuan if the yuan breaches the key 8.2900 resistance level."
Dealers said they expected the yuan to experience a technical correction on Thursday.
The yuan closed lower at 7.2950 from 7.2511 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly down at an intraday high of 1.0696 from 1.0692 against the Hong Kong dollar.
